title: Short and Long Billing Cycles in the Small Business Electricity Supply Multi-Site Credit
content:
Utility meter read schedules make some billing cycles shorter or longer than a month. For the Small Business Electricity Supply multi-site credit, the credited cycle's first day and last day are read from the agreement's latest energy line, and the cycle's days are counted from its first day to its last day, both days included. A cycle of more than 31 days is credited in proportion to its length, the amount being multiplied by its number of days and divided by 30; a cycle of fewer than 25 days is credited at one half (0.5 of the amount); a cycle of 25 to 31 days is credited in full.

## Counting the days

The first day and the last day both count. A hypothetical cycle running 1 March to 1 April has 32 days; one running 3 February to 26 February has 24 days.

## Effect by cycle length

| Days in the credited cycle | Effect on the amount |
|---|---|
| more than 31 | multiplied by the number of days and divided by 30 |
| 25 to 31 | in full |
| fewer than 25 | one half |

## Both sides of each boundary

| Days | Effect |
|---|---|
| 24 | one half |
| 25 | in full |
| 31 | in full |
| 32 | multiplied by 32 and divided by 30 |

## Hypothetical figures

| Amount before the cycle-length effect | Days | Amount after it (unrounded) |
|---|---|---|
| 8.25 USD | 33 | 8.25 multiplied by 33 and divided by 30, that is 9.075 USD |
| 8.25 USD | 22 | 4.125 USD |
| 8.25 USD | 30 | 8.25 USD |
